skill.name: recoup-roster-manage-artist
skill.description: Work inside one artist's folder — read and update their context, brand, songs, and releases. Use for "organize [artist]'s files", "update [artist]'s brand/context", "what's in [artist]'s workspace", or any task about a named artist's files. To list your whole roster use recoup-roster-list-artists; for research/metrics on an artist use recoup-research-artist-overview.
skill.summary: Manage an existing artist workspace, including context, audience, songs, releases, and related Git history.
skill.author: recoupable

security_audit.summary: All eight static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline-code formatting, not Ruby or shell execution. The skill does authorize filesystem changes and Git commits, creating a legitimate medium-impact mutation risk that requires user oversight.

remediation.issue: The skill can modify source-of-truth artist files and create Git commits without requiring explicit approval.
remediation.suggestion: Show the proposed file changes and commit message, then require user confirmation before writing files or committing.

semantic_findings.description: The skill authorizes updates to source-of-truth artist files and instructs the agent to commit changes. Incorrect use could alter important context or repository history without an explicit approval step.

content.value_statement: Artist files can become inconsistent across context, songs, and releases. This skill organizes and updates one existing artist workspace using defined source-of-truth files.
actual_capabilities: Locates an existing artist workspace by artist slug.
Reads artist identity from the RECOUP.md frontmatter.
Organizes artist, audience, image, song, and release files.
Updates static artist context only when the requested information has changed.
Archives time-bound research and release documents when they become stale.
Creates descriptive Git commits that record what changed and why.
limitations: It manages one existing artist workspace and does not create a roster.
It does not perform artist research or retrieve performance metrics.
It requires real source material and must not generate placeholder artist data.
It depends on other Recoup skills for roster listing and platform verification.

use_cases.title: Maintain Artist Context
use_cases.description: Update verified artist and audience details while preserving stable source-of-truth documents.

use_cases.title: Organize Release Materials
use_cases.description: Place songs, release documents, and approved images into the expected workspace structure.

use_cases.title: Audit an Artist Workspace
use_cases.description: Review existing files, identify stale documents, and summarize missing real materials.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect an Artist Workspace
prompt_templates.prompt: Show what is currently stored for [artist name]. Summarize identity, context, audience, songs, releases, and missing expected materials without changing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one existing artist workspace

prompt_templates.title: Add Verified Artist Materials
prompt_templates.prompt: Add these verified materials to [artist name]'s workspace: [materials]. Use the expected folders, avoid placeholders, and show proposed changes before writing.

prompt_templates.title: Update Source-of-Truth Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Update [artist name]'s artist or audience context using this verified information: [details]. Explain each change and preserve unrelated content.
prompt_templates.scenario: Controlled revision of stable artist information

prompt_templates.title: Reconcile and Commit Workspace Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [artist name]'s workspace against current materials. Propose stale-file archives, context updates, and a precise commit message. Wait for approval before changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workspace maintenance with Git history

output_examples.input: What is in Maya River's workspace?
output_examples.output: Maya River has an identity file, artist context, audience context, two songs, and one release document. No approved face guide is present.

output_examples.input: Add the approved single and release notes for Northline.
output: Proposed: add the supplied audio file under the song slug.
Proposed: add the supplied notes as the release master document.
No files changed. Approval is required before writing.

output_examples.input: Refresh Juniper Vale's audience profile with these verified notes.
output_examples.output: The proposed update adds the verified audience regions and platform preferences. Existing artist identity and unrelated audience details remain unchanged.

best_practices: Confirm the artist identity and workspace path before reading or changing files.
Use verified source material and omit sections that lack real information.
Review diffs and obtain approval before updating source-of-truth files or creating commits.
anti_patterns: Do not create an artist workspace when the roster cannot be verified.
Do not insert placeholder names, identifiers, assets, or release details.
Do not overwrite artist or audience context as part of unrelated maintenance.

faq.question: Can this skill create a new artist?
faq.answer: No. It manages an existing artist workspace. Use the appropriate roster onboarding skill to create or verify an artist.

faq.question: Which files are treated as source-of-truth context?
faq.answer: The artist and audience context documents are stable sources used by other skills. Changes should be deliberate and verified.

faq.question: Can it add songs and release documents?
faq.answer: Yes. It can organize supplied audio and release materials under the documented artist workspace structure.

faq.question: Does it research artist metrics?
faq.answer: No. Use the artist overview research skill for metrics and external research.

faq.question: Will it generate missing details?
faq.answer: No. It must use real content and leave unsupported sections absent rather than create placeholders.

faq.question: Does it create Git commits?
faq.answer: The skill instructs the agent to record changes in Git. Users should review the diff and commit message before approval.
